put.description: Stages one immutable verified object in the publisher's one-hour session. conanmanifest.txt is the visibility signal: validates every declared MD5 tree entry, hash revision and package identity, then atomically commits revision metadata, session state and a publish audit for the actual commit caller, using the same validator and commit boundary as management publication. The session version fences concurrent staged-pointer changes. Repeating identical bytes preserves the visible identity; changed bytes conflict. Limits are 1 GiB per object and expanded tree including tar framing, 1 MiB manifest/conaninfo and 4096 manifest/archive entries. Sessions do not expose partial revisions. Applies existing quota, scan and quarantine.

post.description: Administrator-only Nexus 3 read-only source. Credentials are encrypted using GATEWAY_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY; responses and audits never include them. No source writes or target mutations occur. Fetches only credential-visible repositories and their supported read-only configuration. It does not prove global inventory completeness. A failed request is a problem response, never an empty success.

Administrator-only Nexus 3 read-only source. Credentials are encrypted using GATEWAY_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY; responses and audits never include them. No source writes or target mutations occur. Exhausts asset pagination for selected supported Hosted repositories with bounded requests (128), response bytes (16 MiB total, 2 MiB per response), repositories (500) and time (30 seconds). Cyclic tokens, untrusted download URLs and exhausted budgets fail explicitly without partial success. Proxy/Group/unknown formats and Maven SNAPSHOT repositories are explicitly unsupported for asset discovery. MIXED repositories return release-version paths; SNAPSHOT paths, shared metadata and unclassifiable Maven paths are listed explicitly in unsupportedAssets. Budgets count both supported and unsupported assets.

Administrator-only Nexus 3 read-only source. Credentials are encrypted using GATEWAY_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY; responses and audits never include them. No source writes or target mutations occur. Validates explicit native target names, formats/types, existing-name conflicts and ordered Group member mappings. Re-reads source configuration; performs no target writes. Permissions, credentials and source-specific fields require manual reconfiguration.

get.description: Returns repositories for which the authenticated principal has read access. Administrators see the full catalog; a pending or password-change account receives `403` instead. The filter runs on the server, so the result never reveals the existence of a repository the caller cannot read.

Lists repository grant records across repositories for the administrator console. A platform administrator sees every repository; any other caller sees only the repositories it administers, so a repository it cannot administer contributes no rows and is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

Lists logical capacity snapshots across repositories for the administrator console. A platform administrator sees every repository; any other caller sees only the repositories it administers, so a repository it cannot administer contributes no rows and is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

Lists the newest lifecycle jobs across repositories for the administrator console. A platform administrator sees every repository; any other caller sees only the repositories it administers, so a repository it cannot administer contributes no rows and is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

delete.description: Disables the repository. Requires repository `admin` scope, because stopping reads and writes for every client is a repository-administration action rather than a content mutation; a `write` scope is not sufficient.

patch.description: Updates repository configuration. Requires repository `admin` scope, because endpoint, allowlist, egress, upstream credential, anonymous-read, and strict-publication settings change how the repository behaves for every client; a `write` scope is not sufficient.

post.description: Probes the repository's egress path to its upstream using the stored egress proxy configuration. The repository's administrators may do this; the result is ephemeral and never persisted.

Creates or replaces a single grant identified by its principal and resource prefix, leaving every other grant of the repository untouched. Unlike replaceGrants no If-Match is required, because the write is confined to one grant row and cannot clobber concurrent changes to other principals. Returns the full grant list with the new version, exactly like replaceGrants.

delete.description: Removes a single grant identified by principal and optional resource prefix, leaving every other grant of the repository untouched. Answers 404 when no such grant exists, so a console working from a stale list learns the row is already gone. The parameters deliberately carry no length cap beyond a non-empty principal, because the request only has to name a stored row and a row written by an earlier revision must stay removable even when its key is longer than today's write rules allow.

/repositories/{repositoryId}/quarantine-.description:
Versioned, default-off read enforcement for supported Hosted formats.
For APT Hosted, quarantined pool GET/HEAD and complete signed metadata views
containing that package return 403, including retired by-hash views.
Signed bytes are never filtered or rewritten on read. Release restores access
only to existing lifecycle references and never reverses deletion.

post.summary: Create or replay an immutable artifact replication plan
post.description:
Newly accepted plans persist both the immutable source coordinate and
digest; neither field may be present without the other. A request-time
quarantine denial returns 403 without creating a plan. If the final
worker check instead observes quarantine, it parks the existing plan
without publishing target metadata. After release, replaying the exact
request with the same Idempotency-Key requeues and returns that plan; it
does not create a second plan. A PyPI source version whose file membership
changes after enqueue is likewise parked with
`replication_snapshot_changed`; exact replay atomically refreshes that
plan's checkpoints before requeueing the same plan ID.

200.description:
Replication plans involving this repository. Coordinate and digest
are both present for current plans and both absent only on historical
plans created before immutable identity persistence was introduced.

Replication plan and checkpoint progress for this repository.
Coordinate and digest are both present for current plans and both
absent only on historical plans created before immutable identity
persistence was introduced. A new worker fails closed rather than
publishing a non-terminal historical plan with both fields absent.

delete.summary: Cancel a pending or failed replication plan
delete.description:
Stops a pending or failed replication plan from being claimed again. A
running plan cannot be cancelled because the worker owns it mid-flight;
such a request fails with 409. Completed and already-cancelled plans are
also not cancellable. The plan record is retained for audit.

post.description: Restores a tombstoned identity under Repository admin permission. For npm, this reuses the original version, warning, manifest and tarball identity; object size/digest and the collection fence are checked before visibility returns, and the actor's restore audit commits with metadata. A version whose collection has started or whose bytes are missing cannot be restored.

409.description: Collection has started or retained object bytes are unavailable

post.summary: Requeue failed artifact intelligence copy jobs
post.description: Requeues up to 100 failed or cancelled intelligence copy jobs for this repository. Running, pending, retrying, and completed jobs are left unchanged. Candidate selection and state reset are atomic.

get.description: Returns operations currently supported by this Hosted repository's format.

get.summary: Explain effective repository access, including denied decisions
get.description: Explain effective repository access. Without actor, explains the authenticated caller; administrators may provide actor and an optional simulated global role. Resource evaluates prefix-scoped grants against a concrete artifact coordinate or path. A non-administrator only receives a decision for a repository it holds read or intelligence authority over at that resource; any other repository answers exactly like one that does not exist.
The platform tier lists every group; any other caller lists the groups whose referenced repositories it all administers. A page may hold fewer items than pageSize while nextPageToken is set.

post.description: A hosted group references repositories, so the platform tier and the administrators of every repository it references may manage it. The refusal names the member that is out of bounds.

get.description: A hosted group references repositories, so the platform tier and the administrators of every repository it references may read it, the same rule that lets them manage it. Any other caller gets 404, as if the group did not exist.

put.description: A hosted group references repositories, so the platform tier and the administrators of every repository it references may manage it, including the members it drops and the ones it adds. The refusal names the member that is out of bounds.

Sources are local candidates, never a prediction of the next protocol hit. Missing cache evidence does not prove an upstream miss. Maven cache records fetched only through this Group require the current authorized resolution scope. Navigation binds identity, member order, repository configuration and grants. Groups with more than 64 configured members are not supported by this endpoint.

If-Match must name the complete current file set. Unyanking clears the reason; archive bytes remain immutable. Mutation and success audit commit together.

Lists visible Conan recipe references in lexical order. The optional q parameter is a reference prefix used for browse and search.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Canonical Raw path. This is a gateway catch-all parameter and may contain one or more slash-separated segments. Unicode and spaces use canonical percent encoding; empty, dot, dot-dot, encoded separators, control characters, bidirectional formatting controls, and non-canonical escapes are rejected.

get.description: Returns Raw bytes for a file path. `.sha256` and `.sha512` suffixes return a derived lowercase hexadecimal checksum plus newline. When the catch-all path ends in `/`, it instead returns a lexicographically ordered listing of visible Hosted assets below that canonical prefix; `n` and `last` control pagination. With an `uploadId`, returns no content and the current Upload-Offset for an open resumable upload rather than artifact bytes. File GET supports a single Range or bounded multipart/byteranges from one immutable object. A Range field accepts at most 8192 bytes and 16 intervals; overlapping, duplicate and adjacent intervals coalesce in ascending order. Valid unsatisfiable intervals are omitted if another interval is satisfiable. Multipart payload is limited to 64 MiB, with at most 32 KiB of framing; these aggregate limits do not restrict a single coalesced interval. Malformed fields, multiple Range field lines, no satisfiable intervals or exceeded limits return 416. A strong matching If-Range enables Range; weak, date or non-matching validators return the full object. Cold Proxy GET fetches and verifies the complete object before applying local ranges; Range and client validators are never forwarded to the upstream.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One bytes range-set, containing at most 16 intervals.

parameters.name: If-Range
parameters.description: The current strong ETag; other values ignore Range.

200.description: Raw bytes or a Raw directory-prefix JSON page

Content-Disposition.description: Present for file and checksum responses; suggests the decoded final path segment as filename.

206.description: One byte interval, or a bounded multipart/byteranges body with per-part Content-Range and Content-Type, exact total Content-Length, and the original object's ETag and Digest. Multipart responses have no top-level Content-Range. Streams use the captured immutable object; an unavailable or interrupted stream truncates the response and never switches to a newly published path reference.

304.description: The requested representation's ETag matches If-None-Match.

416.description: Invalid, wholly unsatisfiable or excessive ranges. Content-Range is bytes */size and no object stream is opened.

head.description: Returns full-object metadata without a body. Range and If-Range are ignored on HEAD. A matching If-None-Match returns 304.

304.description: The requested representation's ETag matches If-None-Match.

put.description:
Standard Raw Hosted write. The request body is stored as immutable verified content and the canonical Raw path is atomically created or replaced; no management publish session is used for Raw. A `.sha256` or `.sha512` target validates that checksum against an existing primary object and returns no content without storing a sidecar asset. With `uploadId` and `complete=1`, appends any final bytes, requires a `Digest: sha-256=<base64>` header, and atomically publishes the resumable upload.
If-Match and If-None-Match (RFC 9110) make a primary-path write or a resumable completion conditional. The Gateway re-evaluates them in the same lock or transaction that replaces the path reference, so of two writers holding the same validator only one succeeds. `If-None-Match: *` creates only when the path has no current asset; `If-Match: *` replaces only an existing asset; an entity-tag list compares against the current digest, accepting both the `"sha256-<hex>"` tag reads return and the `"sha256:<hex>"` tag writes return. If-Match uses strong comparison, so a weak tag never matches. A failed condition answers 412 without the current validator and stores nothing; a failed resumable completion leaves the upload open. If-Unmodified-Since cannot be evaluated atomically and is rejected with 400. A request without these headers keeps the unconditional replacement behavior.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` or a comma-separated list of entity tags the current path reference must match (strong comparison).

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: `*` for create-only, or a comma-separated list of entity tags the current path reference must not match (weak comparison).

201.description: Immutable content stored and the Raw path reference atomically created or replaced

400.description: Malformed If-Match or If-None-Match, or an unsupported If-Unmodified-Since precondition; nothing is stored

412.description: The current path reference does not satisfy If-Match or If-None-Match; the reference is unchanged and a resumable upload stays open

post.description: Starts an atomically invisible Raw Hosted upload. This operation requires `resumable=1`; the returned Location contains the opaque uploadId.

patch.description: Appends bytes to an open Raw upload session. Upload-Offset must equal the current offset and the response returns the next offset.

delete.description: Deletes a committed Raw asset. With an `uploadId`, cancels the corresponding open resumable upload and discards its staged bytes.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Canonical APT catch-all path containing one or more slash-separated segments below dists/ or pool/. Empty, dot, dot-dot, and percent-encoded traversal segments are rejected.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Optional single byte range used to resume package downloads.

delete.description: Deletes an OCI manifest by digest. Deleting by a mutable tag is not supported.

parameters.name: assetPath
parameters.description: Canonical Maven asset path: groupId path, artifactId, version, and filename. This is a gateway catch-all parameter; directly published or strictly committed POMs, component assets, checksums, and generated metadata are readable.

put.description: Standard Maven/Gradle deploy upload. By default the Gateway publishes each verified upload directly so unmodified clients work without a companion call. When Maven strict publication is enabled for the Hosted repository, the request stages the object until coordinate commit. Client checksum sidecars are assertions and client metadata is a compatibility no-op; the Gateway derives authoritative checksums and metadata from verified objects.

201.description: Published directly by default, or staged when Maven strict publication is enabled; an idempotent replay is also accepted

post.description: Used only by Maven Hosted repositories with strict publication enabled. A CI integration, publishing wrapper, or optional Maven/Gradle extension calls it after normal deploy uploads. It is the strict mode coordinate visibility signal; request ordering, checksums, metadata, and quiet time are never completion signals. Repositories using the default direct mode reject this operation with 409 because their verified PUTs are already visible.

parameters.name: modulePath
parameters.description: Catch-all beginning with the case-escaped module path and ending in /@v/list, /@latest, or /@v/<escaped-version>.(info|mod|zip).

get.description: Reads a standard GOPROXY list, latest, info, mod, or zip representation.

head.description: Returns the same headers as GET without the representation body.

put.description: Gateway-specific Go Hosted publication. The catch-all must identify an escaped semantic version with a .zip suffix. The body is validated as a canonical Go module ZIP containing a matching top-level go.mod. The Gateway derives .mod and .info and publishes all representations in one metadata transaction. Identical retries preserve the first publication time; changed bytes at the same module version are rejected.

400.description: Request body could not be read

403.description: Authenticated principal lacks Repository write permission

parameters.description: Catch-all below /cargo/{repository}/. Reads accept config.json, canonical sparse-index paths, api/v1/crates search, and api/v1/crates/{crate}/{version}/download. Hosted writes accept api/v1/crates/new for PUT publication, api/v1/crates/{crate}/{version}/yank for DELETE, and api/v1/crates/{crate}/{version}/unyank for PUT.

put.description: PUT api/v1/crates/new accepts the Cargo length-prefixed publication frame. PUT api/v1/crates/{crate}/{version}/unyank restores version selection. Proxy and Group reject both mutations.

delete.description: DELETE api/v1/crates/{crate}/{version}/yank; Proxy and Group reject writes.

get.description: Lists the package's dist-tags as an object of tag name to version. Hosted repositories read committed tags; Proxy repositories answer from the cached upstream packument with the same revalidation and stale rules as the packument; Groups merge members in Group order, where the first member that defines a tag is authoritative for it. Tags naming a quarantine-blocked or invisible version are omitted.

403.description: Authenticated principal lacks Repository read permission

head.description: Returns the same headers as GET without the body.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Dist-tag name. Names that parse as an npm SemVer range, including wildcard forms such as x.x, x.1, and v*, are refused. A digit prefix alone is allowed: 2026-release, 2026-10-16, 1-canary, and v1-release remain ordinary tags so `<pkg>@<tag>` stays unambiguous.

put.description: Adds or moves a Hosted dist-tag (`npm dist-tag add`). The body is the target version as a JSON string. The store re-checks the target's visibility under the same row locks that tombstone and restore take, so a tag can never be left naming a tombstoned version. Repeating the current state succeeds without a change and is audited with changed=false. Requires Repository write permission.

400.description: The body is not a JSON string naming a valid SemVer version

get.description: Native packument, including per-version deprecated warnings. Hosted answers include _rev from a consistent package/version snapshot. npm 11.6.2 uses ?write=true before deprecate and unpublish. Hosted tombstones suppress the same version in lower-priority Group members. Proxy deprecated fields follow the normal metadata revalidation/cache contract.

403.description: Repository read permission or account state denies access

put.description: npm publish with one tarball attachment, or npm deprecate/undeprecate with a full packument and no attachments. Both require Repository write permission. Metadata changes require current _rev and preserve every visible version, dist-tag and immutable manifest field except deprecated. npm's own SemVer range selection is honored as the exact changed-version set, not reinterpreted as another range language. Messages are plain text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; empty clears. At most 1000 versions per metadata document. One invalid/unknown target rejects the whole mutation. Changes and their actor/version/reason audit commit together. A lost response or stale retry must be resolved by reading current state; old revisions get 409 and never overwrite later publications, tags, deletes or restores.

put.description: npm 11.6.2 single-version unpublish. Requires Repository admin permission, current path/body _rev, and a full packument retaining unchanged version documents. Removed versions become existing lifecycle tombstones; tags are updated in the same transaction. Invalid retained targets reject the complete change. Tarballs remain under retention, object leases, reference-safe reclaim and the existing management restore operation. No Proxy/Group mutation or upstream delete is performed.

delete.description: npm whole-package unpublish or removal of its only remaining version. Requires Repository admin permission and current revision. At most 1000 visible versions are atomically tombstoned with tags and audit; no bytes are physically deleted. Identity reservations prevent republishing even after reclaim. Restore individual versions through the existing /repositories/{repositoryId}/restore management operation before reclaim; restore preserves deprecation and immutable bytes, creates latest only if absent, and does not recreate all removed custom tags.

EgressProxy.description: Per-Proxy-Repository egress network proxy configuration. Only meaningful when the repository type is proxy. `password` is accepted on write (plaintext over TLS) and stored AES-256-GCM encrypted; responses never return it and carry `credentialsConfigured` instead.

mode.description: direct bypasses any proxy (keeping private-address protection); environment follows process HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY; custom uses the per-repository proxy below.

host.description: Custom proxy hostname or IP, without scheme or credentials.

remoteDns.description: socks5 only. When true the proxy resolves the upstream hostname (socks5h); when false the gateway resolves locally and keeps the private-address check.

noProxy.description: Upstream host suffixes or CIDR ranges that bypass the custom proxy and connect directly. Matched against the upstream host, never the proxy host.

credentialsConfigured.description: True when encrypted proxy credentials are stored.

UpstreamAuth.description: Protected upstream credentials for Go, Maven and OCI Proxy repositories. Basic or Bearer authentication targets the bound upstream. When OCI ociBearer is configured, these credentials are sent only to its bound issuer and content requests use the exchanged pull token. Cross-origin redirects strip credentials. Rotation or clear invalidates credential-bound content and token caches. Changing the upstream URL or OCI issuer binding requires a fresh secret or scheme none; stored credentials are never implicitly rebound to a new destination. Other formats reject this field. `secret` is accepted on write over TLS and stored AES-256-GCM encrypted; responses never return it and carry `credentialsConfigured` instead.

scheme.description: none removes any stored credential and reads the upstream anonymously; basic sends an HTTP Basic credential; bearer sends `Authorization - Bearer <secret>`.

username.description: basic only. Upstream account name. Rejected for bearer.

secret.description: Upstream password or token. Write-only; stored encrypted. Omit on update to keep the stored secret only while its scheme and upstream destination binding are unchanged. Both schemes require a secret, so clear a stored credential by setting scheme to none rather than sending an empty secret.

credentialsConfigured.description: True when an encrypted upstream credential is stored.

OCIBearer.description: Optional upstream Bearer challenge exchange for OCI Proxy repositories. Without this configuration content requests use the explicit upstreamAuth setting. The realm and service bind the approved issuer and audience. With this configuration upstreamAuth credentials are sent only to the bound issuer; this object contains no credentials or cached tokens. It does not add the realm to allowedHosts or grant network access. A cross-origin realm still needs explicit permission under the existing egress policy. On update omit the field to preserve it, or send null to clear it. Setting an object replaces both fields together. Hosted and other formats reject this property, including null. Changing this binding while protected upstream credentials are configured requires a fresh upstreamAuth.secret or upstreamAuth.scheme none in the same request.

realm.description: Exact complete HTTPS token-service URL. The first exchange contract rejects userinfo, all query parameters, and fragments.

service.description: Exact challenge audience. At most 256 UTF-8 bytes; no whitespace or control characters.

conan.description: Official Conan 2.21.0 hash-revision upload and read workflow. Register /conan/{repository} as the remote root; the client appends /v1 or /v2. Hosted PUTs reuse durable publication sessions and immutable object intents. Only a complete validated manifest commits a recipe or package revision. Management publication uses the same validator, snapshot fence and atomic revision/session/audit commit; it cannot publish partial revisions. Group and Proxy remotes are read-only. The retired /conan/v2/{repository} layout is not an alias. Conan 1, SCM revisions and optional metadata uploads are unsupported. See docs/conan-native-publication.md for bounds and evidence.
